lines: Fun Libs in there, the word game. I always fill in 'wrench'.
Laughter from the arcade. Somebody filled a good blank.
Someone read a story out loud in there. The whole room laughed.
Marquee lights chasing round. Twenty-two bulbs. I counted.
Back to work past the marquee. It walks me to my door.
Bulb seven on the marquee is a touch slow. Charming. Leaving it.
Kids filling in blanks, giggling. Best noise on the street.
One word at a time in there. Like screws, really.
A kid asked me for a noun. I said 'hinge'. He loved it.
A kid read his Fun Libs story twice. Second time louder.
Lunch walk past the arcade. Quick peek. A small laugh inside.
Another Fun Libs story played. Built at seventeen. Still going.
No marketing, and still the sign lights up. Word gets round.
Marquee jumped. Someone finished a story. Hope it was silly.
Arcade sign flashed. Somebody filled in the blanks. Nice.
Sign lit up. A kid somewhere put 'banana' in every blank.
Busy terrace. Somebody laughed, then the whole table did.
Cups on saucers all round. Like a room full of small bells.
Full terrace. Marcel moves through it like a good cursor.
Busy lunch. I drink fast and give the chair back. Fair.
Marcel carries four plates. Load-bearing arms. Respect.
Crowded table, wobbly leg. I will bring a shim tomorrow.
Busy café. I tuck my feet in. Marcel needs the lane.
Six bells, up the hill. The marquee will wake soon.
Six o'clock bell. Back to the workshop door shortly.
Bell from the old town. Soft. Like a spoon on a cup.
Six from the church. The arcade bulbs keep their own time.
Little crowd at the rail. I will join them. Rail nine.
Busy rail tonight. I shuffle up. Room for one more.
A whole row of elbows on the rail. Good, sturdy rail.
Nobody talks when it gets close. Then everybody does.
The visitors take photos. I just take the ten minutes.
More people than yesterday. The sun has a following.
Everyone lined up along the rail. Like books on a shelf.
Shuffled up to make room for a family. Room for everyone.
Somebody said ooh. Then everyone said ooh. Good review.
A stranger lent me her spot. I said merci. Twice.
Shoulder to shoulder. Nobody in a hurry. Lovely.
Asgeir along the rail. We nod. No need for words.
A gull, out over the water. Hm. Same note as my vice.
Gull. Loud for its size. I know a lathe like that.
A gull called. It sounds like a hinge that wants oil.
One gull, out over the water. Holding a level line.
The gull says evening. I agree. Down tools.
A gull calls the sun down. I will take it from here.
The gull wants my croissant. Odile will know its name.
The gull got here before the post. Early worker.
Kiosk at the end, my house at the very end. Good neighbours.
Kiosk shutter. Good hinges. I checked them once.
Postcards on the rack. One of my workshop. Nice.
The kiosk smells of coffee and fresh print. Good start.
Kiosk shutter down, padlock neat. Sleep well, little kiosk.
Kiosk all shuttered up. Two more doors and I am home.
Kiosk shutter up, papers stacked. I read headlines sideways.
Kiosk coffee in a paper cup. Warms the screwdriver hand.
Bought a pencil at the kiosk. Already sharpened. Lovely.
Newspaper under my arm. The crossword is for lunch.
The kiosk bell rang as I passed. Same note as my kettle.
Lamps up the hill as well. The old town joins in.
The promenade lit itself. No one had to ask.
There they go. One, two, three. Nobody skipped one.
Lamps striking on down the line. Like a good test run.
Whoever wired these did it in order. I approve.
Each lamp waits for the last. Very polite circuit.
Hm. The lamps beat me to it. Ten more minutes.
Lamp nine is my lamp. It came on right above me.
A row of little moons along the rail. Neat spacing.
The promenade just put its necklace on.
That faint tick when they strike. I love that sound.
Lamps on, sea still pink. Best two minutes of the day.
Glass globes, brass caps. Someone polished those. Nice.
The lamp above me hums a little. We hum the same note.
Lamps on. That means tea and the workbench soon.
I counted the lamps once. Lost count at the café. Lovely.
Lamp by the kiosk is always last. Thinks it over first.
Warm white, all in a row. I would not change a bulb.
Hm. That one came on a breath late. I like it best.
Round moon. Perfectly round. Could not turn that on a lathe.
Walking home by moonlight. The cobbles look silver.
Moon on the water, all the way out. Good night, moon.
Moon high. Key in the lock. Home by its light.
A long shadow by moonlight. It walks home with me.
Rail nine soon. The sun and I have an appointment.
Ten minutes to sunset duty. Putting the chisel to bed first.
Leaving the door ajar. Back after the sun has landed.
The light is going gold. That is my cue. Off to the rail.
Back to the workshop door now. Someone always asks what is inside.
Arcade done. Next I stand by my door and say: tomorrow.
Last story, then the workshop. I will hum the punchline.
Last sip. Back to the bench. The glue has had its lunch too.
Merci, Marcel. Back to work before the chair gets too comfy.
One more minute of sun, then back under my good lamp.
Letters in my pocket. Unlocking the workshop in five minutes.
Workshop next. I left a clamp on a glued joint. Should be set.
One last look at the post office sign, then the lathe.
Then the workshop. Toolrails needs a gentle tightening today.
Sun nearly down. Then back to the bench, lamp first.
When the last orange goes, I go. The lamp is waiting.
Back to it soon. I have a hinge in my head. Must not lose it.
Back inside after this. Evening shift, my favourite one.
Tonight I tighten tool search. Right after this pink bit.
Asgeir went by, thinking face on. I let him think.
Asgeir slowed down at my door. Then sped up. Good sign.
Asgeir waved. I lifted my coffee. Meeting over.
Asgeir, walking and thinking. I can tell. Hands behind.
Asgeir passed the arcade. He smiled at it like an old friend.
Asgeir, baguette under the arm. He did not offer. Fair.
Asgeir, coffee in hand. We both nodded at the post box.
Biscuit stopped to sniff my boot. Pine, I expect.
Biscuit, tail like a metronome. Good tempo, that dog.
Biscuit chose the long way. Yusuf agreed. Nice manners.
Salut, Yusuf. Tell Biscuit his bowl stand is nearly done.
Biscuit trotted by. Tail at a perfect right angle.
Little clicks on the stones. Biscuit. Right on time.
Biscuit sat for me. Yusuf looked betrayed. Ha.
Biscuit stopped at the arcade. He likes the beeps.
Odile straightened my collar in passing. Henri did not slow.
Forty-one years of walking together. Not one wobble.
Henri's cane taps in threes. I hum along. He knows.
Bonsoir, Odile. Bonsoir, Henri. Matching hats tonight.
Henri and Odile, heading for their bench. Early seats.
Odile waved at the arcade kids. Henri waved at me. Nice.
Odile pointed at my window box. She approves of the thyme.
Inès, all elbows and purpose. Lap whatever-it-is.
There goes Inès. I get tired just watching. Kindly.
Inès. Steady pace. Like a good motor, but happier.
Inès, flying. I counted three strides. Then she was gone.
Inès ran by. The rail and I keep the slow lane.
Allez, Inès. One more lap, then the rail.
Inès gave me a thumbs up mid-stride. I gave a screwdriver.
Inès, racing the sun again. The sun is losing.
Inès went by in a sea breeze of her own making. Hm.
Léo ran by. His laces are a project for later.
Nine and three quarters, and very fast with all of it.
Léo went by. I will make him a stopwatch box. Wood.
Léo, waving with both hands while running. Brave.
There goes Léo. Ten laps is a lot of fountain.
Léo shouted "hello builder!" mid-lap. Hello, Léo.
Léo, running ahead of bedtime. It always catches up.
{name} went by. I gave a small nod. A good nod.
Hm hm. Hello, {name}. Mind the sawdust on my boots.
There goes {name}. Walking like the day went well.
{name} said hello first. I owe one hello now.
That was {name}. Nice steady walk. Good balance.
Afternoon, {name}. I fixed nothing of yours today. Yet.
Hello, {name}. The marquee is extra bright for you.
Night, {name}. We are the last two lamps out.
Bonjour, {name}. Sit if you like. Chair is level.
{name} passed my table. I lifted the cup. Salut.
{name} said bon appétit. My omelette said thanks.
Bonjour, {name}. The post box and I are both open.
The post office sign blinked. An agent sent a letter. Good form.
A letter went out. No envelope. Still, the sign looks pleased.
Seventeen tools in that post office. I'd like a look in the drawer.
Another one handled. Quiet work. The best kind.
About a hundred providers, one post office. Good junction box.
I build for agents. I still smile when their mail goes out.
The post sign flickered. Like a nod across the street.
Bright sign. An agent sent mail. I tightened a screw. Teamwork.
Post sign glowed gold on gold. A letter caught the evening.
The town is asleep. The post office is not. Good.
Post sign glowed. Somebody's agent answered before lunch.
Sign flared as I reached the box. Someone's agent beat me to it.
I wonder if the agent says please. I bet it says please.
Checking my own post. The agents already checked theirs.
Sign on all night. Somebody trusts their wiring. I approve.
The agents' mail goes in quietly. No queue, no fuss.
The post office. Open all night. Like my lamp.
Mail for AI agents, in a building with a red box. Lovely.
Post office sign glowing steady. Like a pilot light. Cosy.
Off to lunch past the post office. Its sign gives me a nod.
Post office first. Workbench second. Order matters.
The post office door has a good hinge. Never squeaks. Respect.
Brass letter slot, polished by a thousand hands. Mine too.
Stamps in neat rows behind the glass. Somebody likes a grid.
I hold the door for whoever is next. Mostly the breeze.
Paper smell, ink smell. A nice building to start a day in.
The sign glows a little. An agent is writing early.
Empty promenade. My footsteps sound like a metronome.
Quiet street. I tiptoe past the sleeping windows.
The post office is awake. I am awake. That is everybody.
Not a soul on the promenade. Just me and the lamps.
Can't place the song. Hum it anyway. Close enough.
Old song from somebody's window. I know the chorus. Hum.
Radio through a shutter. Accordion. The arcade beeps along.
The sea is big and simple. I like big and simple.
The water goes from blue to copper. Nobody sanded it.
The sea never needs a second coat. Remarkable.
Light on the water, every ripple a little shaving.
Waves tap the wall below. Steady tempo. I hum along.
Salt on the rail. I wipe a clean spot for my sleeve.
Sea smells of salt and warm stone. Workshop smells of pine.
Gentle swell. Up, down. Like a sanding block, only slower.
A gull glides low over the water. Not one flap. Show-off.
Light skipping on the water. My eyes get the evening off.
Water turning lilac. No lilac paint in the shop. Just looking.
Light on the water makes a road. Right up to my elbows.
Pink on the water now. Commit message: pink.
Every wave has a spark on top. Like a tiny lamp, switched on.
The bay goes quiet just before the sun touches. So do I.
Last bit of gold on the water. Then back to the bench.
Clouds and water, same colour. The seam is invisible.
Sun meets sea. No gap, no overlap. Good joint.
Asgeir at the post office. Checking on the agents too.
Asgeir at the rail, thanking the sun in Norwegian.
Asgeir waves at the sun. The sun goes pink. Polite.
Asgeir walking in the gold light. No hurry. Rare. Good.
Asgeir with a baguette under his arm. He has settled in.
Asgeir at the post office, phone out. Agents wrote back.
Biscuit sniffs every lamp post. Thorough inspector.
Biscuit trotting. Four legs, all in time. Hum.
Camille strolling. She stopped to read the arcade sign.
Camille peering at the arcade. Go in, I want to say.
Camille stopped at my chalk sign. Being built, it says.
Camille steering Léo home. Bedtime. Good luck, Camille.
Camille ordering a niçoise. Looks good. I will copy her.
Camille with a glass at last. Léo asleep, I take it.
Henri and his cane, slow and steady. Right pace for here.
Henri on the evening bench, pointing at lamps one by one.
Henri orders small and strong. So do I. Old habit.
Inès passed twice while I tied one knot. Quick.
Inès, lap after lap. Steady cadence. I like steady.
Inès at the rail, still puffing. Made it in time.
Inès versus the sunset. I am cheering for Inès.
Inès at my table again. Asks what I make. I hum.
Léo trailing Camille home. Asking for five more minutes.
Léo at the café, legs swinging. Chair too tall. Noted.
Marcel slides between chairs like a waxed drawer.
Marcel wipes a table till it shines. I know that feeling.
Marcel with a full tray. Not a drop. Fine balance.
Marcel carrying rosé. Pink glasses, gold light. Nice.
Marcel set my cup down before I sat. Perfect fit.
Marcel is everywhere at noon. Like a good glue.
Odile knows everyone. She waved me over. Five minutes.
Odile on Henri's arm. Two people, one good pace.
Odile watching the promenade like a play. I have a small part.
Odile and the tarte. She saves the crust for last.
Théo still has my screwdriver. He waves it. Fine.
Théo strolling at five. Calls it a meeting. Fair enough.
Théo asking about robot email. I point at the post office.
Yusuf follows Biscuit. Biscuit follows his nose.
Yusuf holding his phone up to the sky. A view for Mum.
Yusuf at the rail. Biscuit sits. We all just watch.
Yusuf and Biscuit on the long round. Biscuit is steering.
Yusuf nods at me. Biscuit nods at my boots. Thank you both.
There. Touchdown. Gentle as a level bubble settling.
Sun on the water. Flat line, round sun. Good geometry.
The sun is on the sea. I stop humming for this bit.
Half a sun now. The sea is holding the other half.
Every evening it lands in the same spot. Reliable.
Sunset. Pencil behind the ear. I just look.
Orange all the way across the bay. Like hot brass.
The sun meets the sea. Nobody on the rail says a word.
Down it goes. Shipped for today.
Elbows on the rail, sun on the sea. My two fixed points.
Slow down, sun. Ah, no. Right on schedule.
Sun on the horizon. Like a coin in a slot. Click.
Last of the sun on my face. Warm as a planed board.
The sea goes gold. The rail goes gold. My hands too.
I always think: now it lights somebody's morning.
Pink, then orange, then one gold line. Lovely finish.
The sea takes the sun very gently. Like a drawer closing.
Merged. Sun into sea. Clean, no conflicts.
The sun is on time again. I could set the lathe by it.
That last bit of sun looks like a hot rivet.
{name} is home. Their window is a warm little square.
One more lit window. {name}. The house looks pleased.
Bonsoir, {name}. Your window lit just as I passed.
{name}'s window, warm yellow. Mine will be next.
A window comes on up the street. Hello, {name}.
There goes {name}'s window. The street fills in.
Workshop sign blinked. Tool search did its job. Hm.
Sign lit. An agent took a tool off my wall. Put it back too.
Somebody's agent used a tool. Through my workshop. I hum louder.
An agent came in for a tool while I stood in the door. Polite.
exchanges: Room for one more. Always room for the builder.
He gets top billing. He insists.
Fine as your joinery, mon cher.
All well. You hummed. So yours too.
Always. Now tell me what the workshop makes.
Steady hands, mon ami. Like yours.
Inès. You ran all that and you are not even puffed.
Puffed inside. Look at that colour, though.
Same water as yesterday, Asgeir. New colours.
Every night a new release. Nydelig.
Morning, Asgeir. The post office kept its lights on for you.
It always does. Very loyal building.
Back to work in a minute, Marcel. Lovely soup.
Go, go. Your lamp misses you more than I do.
Last sip. Workshop next. Merci for the shade.
The chair will be warm for you tomorrow, mon ami.
Post sign glowed, Marcel. Agent mail at lunch.
A letter before dessert. Very civilised, mon ami.
Lamps coming on. Left to right, like a loop.
Eleven! I counted every single one. Done!
There. The lamps. Whoever wired them was patient.
Every night, right on time. I want that for my code.
The lamp by your bench just lit, Henri.
Forty years it has lit my crossword. Faithful.
Odile, look. One lamp, then the next.
Like pearls on a string, chéri. Every evening.
Sun is touching the water. Down tools.
Three, two, one... in! Perfect landing.
There it goes. Into the bay.
Ha det, sol. See you over the hill tomorrow.
Sun on the water. Hold still, everyone.
Hold still? At my age, that is my best trick.
Half a sun left. A good half.
The better half, chéri. Like Henri.
Good crowd at the rail tonight. Elbow to elbow.
Fourteen people and one dog. A record!
Everyone came out. Nobody was told to.
Best kind of meeting. No agenda, one sun.
Sea's flat as a fresh-planed board.
Blikkstille, we say. Flat calm. Same idea.
Hear that gull, Henri? Same one as yesterday.
That is Gaston. He has opinions about bread.
Asgeir two posts down. Same elbows, same rail.
Same sun too. We could start a small club.
Henri on his bench, hat tipped. Ready for the show.
Front row, mon ami. I booked it forty years ago.
Last bit of pink. Then back to the lathe.
Go! I will finish watching it for you.
Sun's down. The workbench is calling.
Go on. I will wave at your lamp from the bench.
Marquee just flashed. Someone finished a story.
Mine, probably. I wrote 'pastis' in every blank.
There. The sign blinked. A new Fun Libs story.
Was it mine? I put 'Léo' in all the blanks!
Sign lit up. Somebody filled in the blanks.
Léo did one this morning. The hero was a croissant.
Arcade bulbs warming up. Good old wiring.
I am researching. For work. Very important research.
Church bell. Six. Right on time, that clock.
Six! The rail, then. Léo will be waving already.
Six bells from the old town. Soft today.
Six. Officially rosé o'clock. The bell agrees.
Camille, peeking at the arcade again.
Just looking! Léo says the top score is his.
Théo. Phone in hand. Working hard, I see.
Very hard. I am answering a sunset.
Sign flared. An agent just picked a tool.
The right one, by the look of it. It glows smug.
There. The sign. Somebody's agent borrowed a tool.
Biscuit wagged at it. He likes things that light up.
Workshop sign just lit. Toolrails at work.
Lovely glow! Cannot stop! Keep building!
There goes Biscuit. Tail like a metronome.
Yusuf and Biscuit. The long evening round.
Long one. He wants to say hello to your door.
Full terrace. Every chair doing its job.
Twelve chairs, twelve people! I checked!
Busy today. Marcel is doing the tray waltz.
Un, deux, trois, cups! Your espresso, mon ami.
Last sip. Then back to the clamps.
Go! Back by half one. Very efficient!
Henri across the way. Small, strong coffee, I bet.
Small, strong, and slowly. Like good work.
That gull has his eye on Odile's tarte.
He may look, chéri. He may not touch.
Léo is on his second citron pressé.
Third. He calls it research. Like his father.
Post office sign brightened. An agent sent a letter.
Even the robots answer email before me. Bravo.
Théo, two baguettes. One already shorter.
The short one is a sample. Quality control.
Post office humming. Never shuts, that place.
Like my coffee machine. We are colleagues.
Full terrace. Good thing we have our table.
Our table. Marcel guards it with a saucer.
Same table, same cup, same builder. Voilà.
